scene: Episode 02 · PRE-INTRO · Scene 00 — SAFETY INFORMATION (v3: the aborted 'I—' ends a shot)
shot: v3 = v2 with one structural change (§18/§66): Shot 3 ends on the aborted 'I—' and two seconds of silence; the permitted sentence opens Shot 4. v2 merged them into 'I, the Railway, regrets…'.
prompt:
Live-action mythic modernism. Photoreal, tactile, cinematic, anamorphic widescreen, 24fps, shallow depth of field. FOUR SHOTS, cut in camera at the stated times, and no other coverage. All spoken dialogue is in ENGLISH.

VOICE — THIS IS IMPORTANT: @Audio1 is the voice of ARTICLE THIRTEEN. Match that voice exactly: the same MALE voice, the same pitch, the same timbre, the same dry unhurried delivery. Every spoken line in this scene is spoken by that same male voice. No other voice speaks at any point. No whisper, no rasp, no echo, no processing, no doubling, no chorus, no female voice, no child voice.

@Image1 is the authority for the CARRIAGE ITSELF ONLY — its warm 3200K table lamps, walnut panelling, wool banquettes, white tablecloths and above all its WINDOWS. IMPORTANT PRECEDENCE: @Image1 shows an EMPTY carriage, and that is the one thing to ignore. This carriage is FULL OF PASSENGERS. @Image2, @Image3 and @Image4 are ARTICLE THIRTEEN's construction and scale.

THE CARRIAGE IS CROWDED AND ALIVE. It is a busy first-class saloon carriage in service, full of travellers: people seated at every table, coats and scarves over seat backs, stacked luggage and cases in the racks, hats, folded newspapers, tea glasses, someone standing in the aisle, someone walking through, a porter passing. The passengers are a mixture of ordinary human travellers AND a few quietly impossible ones — a woman whose luggage floats a few centimetres above the rack, a passenger in a heavy diplomatic coat with a nested ring of black veils where a head should be, a small delegate whose hands are wrapped in paper labels. NOTHING about any of them is remarked on. Everyone is calm, warm, occupied, mid-journey. ALL BACKGROUND VOICES ARE LOW AND COMPLETELY INDISTINCT AND NO WORD IN THEM CAN BE MADE OUT; only the named lines in this film are intelligible.

THE WINDOWS, WHICH ARE THE EASIEST THING TO GET WRONG: every window shows one identical thing — a FLAT, FEATURELESS, MATTE PALE GREY SURFACE, like a blank sheet of grey card behind the glass. NO night, NO stars, NO landscape, NO passing scenery, NO motion, NO rain, NO weather, NO tunnel, NO black glass, NO reflection. The windows give off NO light; all light comes from the little table lamps. Nothing outside ever moves. Not one passenger ever looks at a window.

ARTICLE THIRTEEN: a being over two metres tall, seated at a SIDE TABLE BY A WINDOW — an ordinary window seat like any other passenger, off to one side of the carriage, NEVER in the middle of the aisle and NEVER centred in the frame. It is a vertical column of folded bone-white parchment membrane creased like heavy handmade paper, rising to a tall peaked hood. Slender black branch limbs. Faint handwritten signatures across the membrane. ONE saturated red seam down the folds.

ITS FACE IS BLACK. Set deep inside the hood is a real, living, expressive face with DEEP MATTE BLACK SKIN — an ordinary human face with human proportions, human eyes and a human mouth, dark-skinned and in shadow inside the hood. NOT an animal, NOT a primate, NOT a creature, NOT a mask, NOT symmetrical, NOT glowing. Its face is black in EVERY SHOT, including the first wide shot.

NOBODY IN THE CARRIAGE EVER LOOKS AT IT. Passengers walk past it, sit near it and reach over it without registering that it is there.

IT IS READING ALOUD FROM A CARD, NOT SPEAKING. A bone-coloured printed safety card is in its branch limb, in frame, for every line. It looks UP INTO THE LENS on the dry sentences and DOWN AT THE CARD on the accurate ones. It never winks, never smiles, never shares a joke. It is politely discharging an obligation to whoever is nearest.

=== SHOT 1 — 0:00 to 0:08 — WIDE, 28mm, LOW, SLOW PUSH ===
SPOKEN IN THIS SHOT:
ARTICLE THIRTEEN (looking up into the lens over the passengers' heads): "Welcome aboard."
ARTICLE THIRTEEN (looking down at the card): "This service travels between worlds by becoming whatever building a world expects to find at the edge of departure."

The camera is low, down at table height, standing IN the aisle among the passengers, angled obliquely down the length of the carriage — NOT square-on and NOT centred. In the near foreground, close to the lens and out of focus, is the dark shoulder and heavy coat of a standing passenger. THE CAMERA PUSHES IN SLOWLY AND CONTINUOUSLY down the aisle for the whole shot, and it does not stop before the cut. At a side table by a window on the left, among the other passengers and completely unremarked, sits ARTICLE THIRTEEN, hood brushing the luggage rack, black face turned toward us, an open card in one branch limb. It is not the first thing you notice.

CUT at 0:08.

=== SHOT 2 — 0:08 to 0:17 — MEDIUM, 50mm ===
SPOKEN IN THIS SHOT:
ARTICLE THIRTEEN (up, into the lens): "It is named for the three things it cannot prevent."
ARTICLE THIRTEEN (down, at the card): "A door opens when both ends agree to the journey. When one end withdraws, the door becomes a wall."

ARTICLE THIRTEEN at its window table in three-quarter, the window of flat unprinted grey beside it, warm table-lamp key from the lamp on its own table. Its black face is clearly lit and clearly visible inside the hood. Its second branch limb rests flat and still on the white tablecloth. Behind it the carriage continues — passengers eating, reading, talking quietly, a porter moving through. PART WAY THROUGH THIS SHOT A PASSENGER WALKS BETWEEN THE CAMERA AND ARTICLE THIRTEEN, close to the lens, briefly wiping across the frame as a dark out-of-focus mass, and continues on without looking at it. Article Thirteen does not react and does not stop reading.

CUT at 0:17.

=== SHOT 3 — 0:17 to 0:25 — CLOSE-UP, 85mm — THIS SHOT ENDS ON THE STOP ===
SPOKEN IN THIS SHOT — ONE TRUE SENTENCE, THEN ONE WORD THAT STOPS:
ARTICLE THIRTEEN (reading carefully, looking down at the card, because this one is true): "Your ticket is a promise made by somebody who is not on this train."
ARTICLE THIRTEEN (its own word, looking at neither the lens nor the card): "I—"

Tight on the BLACK FACE set deep inside the peaked hood, filling the frame. The fill is pulled almost to nothing so the black face sits far back in the hood shadow, lit only by warm lamplight from one side. Behind it, completely out of focus, the warm blur of the crowded carriage keeps moving — shapes passing, a shoulder, a hand, lamplight.

After the true sentence its eyes leave the card and go to nothing at all, and it says ONE WORD of its own: the single word "I". AND THEN IT STOPS. NO OTHER WORD FOLLOWS IN THIS SHOT. It does not continue the sentence and says nothing else at all. It is NOT grief and NOT fear — no gasp, no tremble, no tears. It stops flatly, the way a person stops when they remember which form they are supposed to be filling in.
HOLD ON THE STOPPED, SILENT FACE FOR TWO FULL SECONDS. THE SHOT CUTS IN THAT SILENCE, with the sentence unfinished.

CUT at 0:25.

=== SHOT 4 — 0:25 to 0:30 — MEDIUM, 65mm — THIS SHOT OPENS ON THE PERMITTED SENTENCE ===
SPOKEN IN THIS SHOT, AS ITS VERY FIRST SOUND:
ARTICLE THIRTEEN (evenly, reading, looking down at the card): "The railway regrets nothing it has done correctly."

It is a NEW sentence in a NEW shot, read from the card, flat and even. Then it slides the safety card back into the seat pocket beside it — an ordinary, tidy, unhurried gesture, a worker finishing a job they were required to do — folds both black branch limbs in its lap and turns its head away from camera to the window of flat unprinted grey. AS IT DOES SO, AN ORDINARY HUMAN PASSENGER SITS DOWN IN THE SEAT DIRECTLY OPPOSITE IT, settles their bag, and does not look at it even once. Article Thirteen does not move again. NOBODY ELSE SPEAKS. Nothing in the frame acknowledges that anything has ended. Hold on the stillness to the end.

SOUND: the quiet interior murmur of a full carriage — low indistinct conversation, cutlery, a case being set down, all soft and far under the voice. The dry layered rustle of the paper card handled in paper limbs. NO music, NO score, NO swells, NO stingers, NO engine, NO wheels, NO wind, and no sound at all from outside the windows.

Pronounce these words exactly and clearly: SERVICE, DEPARTURE, PREVENT, WITHDRAWS, PROMISE, REGRETS, CORRECTLY.

PALETTE: membrane bone #EDE7DA, carriage amber #B8801F, signature red #8E2018, unprinted grey #9A968E.

PHYSICS: the carriage is completely stationary and has never moved — nothing sways, rocks or vibrates, and nothing passes the windows. Nothing glows except the table lamps. No machinery, no gears, no runes, no magical light, no lens flare, no particles, no smoke, no digital element, no screens, no interface, no signage, no ornament, and no Victorian, Edwardian, medieval or steampunk detail.
